quotes.speaker: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II
quotes.quote: My high school game was like Draymond Green. But goddammit! I'm not dissing Draymond. He's a four-time fucking champion! I know he's not dissing me. Five days ago, Draymond was like, you know, people come up right. He was business as usual. You see that? Some woman told him, 'You know what? My son loves you!' He's like, 'Well, your son was ass.' He plays just like you. He said, 'Well, your son must be ass.'
quotes.why_it_matters: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II humorously compares his high school basketball game to Draymond Green, highlighting a self-aware, all-around style of play.

quotes.speaker: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II
quotes.quote: I was a 4.0 student. And so I was always in the games, I was always trying to do what the coaches told me to do. In open gym, I was solid. In practice, I was solid. But when I got in the game, man, my nerves were too bad. The lights, my nerves were too bad.
quotes.why_it_matters: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II shares his experience with performance anxiety in high-stakes games despite strong practice, offering insight into the mental challenges even talented players face.

quotes.speaker: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II
quotes.quote: Oh man, I mean, I think it's in the water, man. I just think it's, it's really about the pride. I think people out there who come from Oakland, they're real grounded. Myself, Mahershala, Ryan, Dame, Mahershala, Tom Hanks, he cool. He solid. And sometime I be sitting back and I be like, why is that? But I know why it is, because I think you kind of gotta be. If you kind of picking up what I'm putting down, you kind of gotta be. And I think that gives us a lot of time to focus on our craft, to keep the main thing the main thing. And I think that, I really do think that that helps a lot.
quotes.why_it_matters: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II attributes the grounded nature and focus of Oakland-bred talent, including himself and other notable figures, to the city's unique environment, suggesting a strong work ethic and dedication to craft.
